description: OrchestrANT's Renovate config. Everything shared with the rest of the family comes from ContainerHub's preset; only the rules that are genuinely specific to THIS repo are restated below.

The single biggest thing the preset buys this repo is the git-submodules manager: Renovate disables it by default, which is why third_party/ContainerHub has never been watched by anything. The Windows and Linux lanes are consumed from that pin, so a stale gitlink is the difference between running the hub's current gates and running whatever they looked like when the pin was last touched by hand.

ORDERING: Renovate resolves `github>Kataglyphis/ContainerHub` from ContainerHub's DEFAULT BRANCH. The preset (ContainerHub default.json) must be merged there before this file resolves; until then Renovate reports a config error on this repo rather than silently running with defaults.
Dependabot: .github/dependabot.yml is deliberately still present. See the comment at the top of that file for why it is not deleted in the same change.

Renovate's pre-commit manager is DISABLED BY DEFAULT, and enabledManagers does not override that -- a run with enabledManagers:[pre-commit] still logs "pre-commit is disabled" and extracts fileCount 0 / depCount 0 (measured, renovate 44.71.0, 2026-09-10). So .pre-commit-config.yaml has never been read here.

That made the packageRule below half dead: it deliberately lists `astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit`, the name only this manager produces, so that the rev in .pre-commit-config.yaml could not drift away from the `ruff` pin in pyproject.toml unattended. With the manager off, the rev was not held back -- it was invisible. It sat at v0.16.4 while v0.16.7 was published.

Enabling it here rather than in ContainerHub's preset is temporary: this is the only repo in the family whose .pre-commit-config.yaml declares a remote `repo:` with a rev. BeschleunigerBallett's and AccelerANTgine's declare only `repo: local` hooks, which carry no version to bump. It belongs in the shared preset once that file is free to edit.

Pins that mirror a ContainerHub versions.env key are notification-only. Bumping them here alone is exactly the drift this repo just fixed: ruff sat at 0.15.21 in uv.lock and v0.13.2 in .pre-commit-config.yaml while the hub graded the Linux lane with RUFF_VERSION=0.16.4, so the same tree could pass locally and fail in CI.

A bump therefore needs the human ritual - move versions.env in ContainerHub first, then pyproject.toml, .pre-commit-config.yaml and `uv lock` here in one change. dependencyDashboardApproval still SHOWS the update; it only refuses to open the PR unattended.

matchDepNames MUST list every SPELLING of those pins, because the name is the manager's, not the package's. ruff appears twice under two different names: the pep621/uv manager reads pyproject.toml and reports `ruff`, while the pre-commit manager reads .pre-commit-config.yaml and reports the REPOSITORY, `astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit`, from the github-tags datasource. Listing only `ruff` left the .pre-commit-config.yaml rev free to be bumped unattended - i.e. it left open the exact half of the ruff drift the prose above describes. uv.lock needs no entry of its own: Renovate refreshes it as part of the pyproject.toml update rather than treating it as a separate dependency.

ONNXRUNTIME_GENAI_VERSION is pinned under two distribution names here - `onnxruntime-genai` in the ml-ai extra and `onnxruntime-genai-cuda` in gpu/gpu-nvidia - and both must move together. `onnxruntime-genai-directml` is deliberately NOT listed: it carries no `==` pin (PyPI ships no wheel at the hub version), so there is no pinned version for Renovate to bump and a row here would match nothing.

torch and torchvision are pinned FOUR times in pyproject.toml - once in each of the pytorch-cpu, pytorch-cu130, pytorch-rocm71 and pytorch-custom extras - and [tool.uv.sources] routes the first three to a DIFFERENT index each (download.pytorch.org/whl/{cpu,cu130,rocm7.1}). Renovate cannot model that fan-out: pep621's uv processor collapses all three index URLs into one registryUrls list on a single `torch` dependency, the pypi datasource merges their release lists, and the highest version across the union then wins for every one of the four occurrences at once.

Measured 2026-09-10, renovate 44.71.0, real config with every manager enabled: all four `torch==2.13.0` occurrences got the SAME proposal, `==2.14.0+cu130`, taken from registryUrl https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 - a CUDA 13.0 build, proposed for the pytorch-cpu and pytorch-rocm71 extras as well. torchvision was identical: `==0.28.0` -> `==0.29.0+cu130`. The pins are written as plain versions and uv appends the local build tag per index, so a `+cu130` value is the wrong SHAPE in every one of the four places, not just the wrong number.

registryUrls pins the LOOKUP to PyPI, where these projects publish plain releases with no +local tag. It does not change where uv installs from - [tool.uv.index] and [tool.uv.sources] are untouched - only which release list Renovate compares against. Measured after: `==2.13.0` -> `==2.14.0` and `==0.28.0` -> `==0.29.0`, which is the shape the pins already use and is valid in all four extras. Two other candidates were measured and rejected: no override gives `+cu130`, and pinning the lookup to the cpu index gives `==2.14.0+cpu` - still a local tag, still wrong for three extras.

dependencyDashboardApproval is the second half and is NOT redundant, because the accelerator indexes do not publish in step. Measured the same day, straight off the indexes: PyPI and whl/cpu and whl/cu130 all carry torch 2.14.0 and torchvision 0.29.0, while whl/rocm7.1 stops at torch 2.13.0+rocm7.1 and torchvision 0.28.0+rocm7.1. So the update Renovate now proposes correctly is one this repo still cannot take: `uv lock` for the ml-ai-rocm / pytorch-rocm71 extra would fail to resolve it. Renovate cannot see that - it compares one merged release list - so the decision stays human, and the dashboard is where it gets surfaced.

`triton-rocm` is deliberately NOT listed, for the same reason onnxruntime-genai-directml is left out of the rule above: it carries no `==` pin (uv resolves it from the rocm index and only uv.lock records 3.7.1), so there is no pinned version to bump and a row here would match nothing. Measured: it extracts with skipReason=unspecified-version.

The riscv64 rows - `torch @ git+https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch.git@v2.13.0` and the vision equivalent - are matched by this rule but are inert either way: pep621 gives them skipReason=invalid-value and never looks up a candidate. They move by hand with the pins above them.

The matcher was proved rather than assumed: the same matchManagers/matchDepNames pair carrying `enabled: false` instead removed exactly the torch and torchvision entries from the lookup (skipReason=disabled) and left ruff, onnxruntime-genai and the rest untouched.
